overall: The AG found the Committee did not violate the Open Meeting Law: the three litigation-related executive sessions fell under Purpose 3, so no Purpose 1 notice to the complainant or his wife was required. The AG added a reminder on minutes detail, with no order.

allegations.summary: Committee allegedly met in executive session three times to discuss the complainant and his wife without giving them prior notice of those discussions.
allegations.key_passage: Instead, all three executive sessions were used to discuss ongoing litigation matters and were therefore appropriate under Purpose 3.

allegations.summary: AG reviewed the sparse executive session minutes in camera and reminded the Committee of its duty to keep minutes detailed enough for a non-attendee to understand what occurred.
allegations.key_passage: A public body is required to create meeting minutes with sufficient detail and accuracy so that a member of the public who did not attend the meeting could read the minutes and have a clear understanding of what occurred.

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
